findings.title: No retry on 401 removes the re-read that ran after AccountProvider cleared a stale Bearer token
findings.body:
Observed: the engine authenticates with only the Bearer token when one is present. In `engine/api/src/platform/auth/platform-auth.service.ts:1833-1843`, `resolveActorFromRequestToken` returns `authenticateFromToken(token)` and checks cookies only when there is no token. On a 401, `AccountProvider` (`console/contexts/account-context.tsx:51-58`) calls `unsetToken()` and `unsetImpersonationToken()`. Before this change, SWR's default retry ran `GET /account` again 5–15 s later. That request went out without the Bearer header, so a valid BetterAuth cookie returned 200 and the person was signed in again. `shouldRetryOnError: (error) => error.status !== 401` removes that re-read.

What follows from this: an impersonation token lives 24 h in localStorage (`expiresIn = 86400`, platform-auth.service.ts:2898; set by `routes/Admin/PlatformUsers/Detail.tsx:165` and `JobsManagement.tsx:88`). Take an operator who still holds an expired one and opens a public `resolveAccount` page (`/offers/*/*`, `/start`, `/agreements/*`). They now stay signed out on that page until the next focus, reconnect or reload. `OfferSiteHeader` shows "Log in", and the StartPage views show the visitor state. Before, the person came back within seconds. Private routes are not affected: `RouteAuthBoundary` already redirected on the first 401, before any retry. The trigger needs an operator holding a stale impersonation token who opens a public offer or agreement link, so impact is limited to an internal user. Any focus or a click on "Log in" fixes it.
findings.fix: Optional. Leave as is and accept recovery on focus. Or, in the 401 branch of the `AccountProvider` effect, call `mutate()` once when `unsetToken`/`unsetImpersonationToken` actually removed a token, so the cookie-only re-read still happens without a retry loop.
